chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Asim ibn Humayn Humayd from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not be surprised by the man who confesses to the blood [killing], for indeed he has at Allah a killer who will not die.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'killer who will not die' mentioned in the hadith about the man who confesses to blood?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) conveys the Prophet’s (s.a.w.s.) warning that a murderer has a divinely appointed, immortal avenger (*qatil la yamut*), emphasizing that divine retribution is not merely physical but spiritual and eternal. This concept underscores the Shia belief in the permanence of the soul's accountability and the specific, unceasing nature of Allah's justice against those who shed blood unjustly. The 'immortal killer' is often interpreted by scholars as either a specific angel, a spiritual entity, or the enduring consequence of the sin itself that pursues the soul beyond death.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “Do not be surprised with a person who  murders  excessively  because  his  killer  is  with  Allah who will never die.”
